From 706b3dc2ac7a998c55e14b3fd2e8f934c367e6e0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:43:15 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] spi: mpc52xx: fix use-after-free on unbind

The state machine work is scheduled by the interrupt handler and
therefore needs to be cancelled after disabling interrupts to avoid a
potential use-after-free.

Fixes: 984836621aad ("spi: mpc52xx: Add cancel_work_sync before module remove")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Pei Xiao <xiaopei01@kylinos.cn>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260414134319.978196-5-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi-mpc52xx.c b/drivers/spi/spi-mpc52xx.c
index 823b49f8ece2..c8c8e6bdf421 100644
--- a/drivers/spi/spi-mpc52xx.c
+++ b/drivers/spi/spi-mpc52xx.c
@@ -519,10 +519,11 @@ static void mpc52xx_spi_remove(struct platform_device *op)
 
 	spi_unregister_controller(host);
 
-	cancel_work_sync(&ms->work);
 	free_irq(ms->irq0, ms);
 	free_irq(ms->irq1, ms);
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&ms->work);
+
 	for (i = 0; i < ms->gpio_cs_count; i++)
 		gpiod_put(ms->gpio_cs[i]);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the `mpc52xx_spi_remove()` function of the MPC52xx SPI driver by reordering the cleanup steps.

### File modified: `drivers/spi/spi-mpc52xx.c`
- **Change**: The call to `cancel_work_sync(&ms->work)` was moved from *before* `free_irq(ms->irq0, ms)` and `free_irq(ms->irq1, ms)` to *after* both `free_irq` calls.

### Relationship between modifications
The order of cleanup operations is critical because the state machine work (`ms->work`) is scheduled by the interrupt handler. Previously, the work was cancelled before disabling the interrupts, which left a window where an interrupt could fire after cancellation and re-schedule the work. This could lead to the work being executed after the IRQ handler or the driver data had been freed, causing a use-after-free. By moving `cancel_work_sync` after `free_irq`, interrupts are first disabled, ensuring no new work can be scheduled, and then any pending work is safely cancelled before the rest of the resources are released.

spi: mpc52xx: fix use-after-free on unbind

The state machine work is scheduled by the interrupt handler and
therefore needs to be cancelled after disabling interrupts to avoid a
potential use-after-free.

Fixes: 984836621aad ("spi: mpc52xx: Add cancel_work_sync before module remove")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Pei Xiao <xiaopei01@kylinos.cn>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260414134319.978196-5-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The state machine work (`ms->work`) was cancelled before disabling interrupts. Since the work is scheduled by the interrupt handler, after cancellation an interrupt could still fire and re-schedule the work. Subsequently, the interrupt handler and driver data are freed, causing a use-after-free when the re-scheduled work executes on the freed resources.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mpc52xx_spi_remove(struct platform_device *op)
 {
 	struct spi_controller *host = spi_controller_get(platform_get_drvdata(op));
 	struct mpc52xx_spi *ms = spi_controller_get_devdata(host);
 	int i;
 
 	spi_unregister_controller(host);
 
-	cancel_work_sync(&ms->work);
 	free_irq(ms->irq0, ms);
 	free_irq(ms->irq1, ms);
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&ms->work);
+
 	for (i = 0; i < ms->gpio_cs_count; i++)
 		gpiod_put(ms->gpio_cs[i]);
 
 	kfree(ms->gpio_cs);
 	iounmap(ms->regs);
 	spi_controller_put(host);
 }

Reason:  
The work `ms->work` is scheduled by the interrupt handler. Cancelling it before disabling interrupts (`free_irq`) leaves a window where an interrupt can still fire and re‑schedule the work after the cancellation. When the device is later removed, the interrupt handler and driver data are freed, causing a use‑after‑free when the re‑scheduled work runs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

```c
cancel_work_sync(&ms->work);
```
Reason:  
By first freeing the interrupts (`free_irq`), no new work can be scheduled by the interrupt handler. Then `cancel_work_sync` safely waits for any already scheduled work to complete. This ordering ensures all resources are still valid during the work’s execution and prevents a use‑after‑free.
